message: Use an adaptive inverse-distance heuristic: each edge receives a higher score when it is short relative to the typical distances from both endpoints, making the rule sensitive to local scale. import numpy as np def heuristics_v2(distance_matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: d = np.asarray(distance_matrix, dtype=float) if d.ndim != 2 or d.shape[0] != d.shape[1]: raise ValueError("distance_matrix must be a square 2D array") if not np.all(np.isfinite(d)): raise ValueError("distance_matrix must contain only finite values") if np.any(d < 0): raise ValueError("distance_matrix must contain non-negative distances") n = d.shape[0] if n == 0: return np.empty_like(d) mask = ~np.eye(n, dtype=bool) positive = d[mask & (d > 0)] eps = np.finfo(float).eps scale = np.median(positive) if positive.size else 1.0 row_values = np.where(mask & (d > 0), d, np.nan) row_scale = np.nanmedian(row_values, axis=1) row_scale = np.where(np.isfinite(row_scale) & (row_scale > 0), row_scale, scale) local_scale = 0.5 * (row_scale[:, None] + row_scale[None, :]) scores = np.exp(-d / (local_scale + eps)) / (d + eps) scores[~mask] = 0.0 maximum = np.max(scores) if maximum > 0: scores /= maximum return scores
